title: Review of c18's shelled Flow-Lenia metabolic cells: Supported for I, M, E, D on fresh seeds 11-13. On all 3 fresh forks the daughter whose food is cut dies, the first two within 140 t. The shell is a set-point readout of the body (B by construction)
summary: A labkit pack of world.py, unchanged, on fresh seeds 11 and 12 (t=800): from the planted patch the shelled gliders divide to generation 5 and 4, with 12 and 8 persistent splits, merge/split 0.76 and 0.86 (reticulate), and 48 and 56 tracks that move at least 1 body length (up to 9.9 and 13.0). tracks.png shows each body inside a closed green S ring, but neighbouring rings often fuse into a network. I also ran c18's dfork.py starve-one-daughter fork on fresh seeds 11, 12 and 13 (300 t after the fork). On seed 11 the starved daughter falls to 19% of its fork matter by t=288 (138 t after the fork), and on seed 12 to 0 by t=284, while in their fed twins the same daughters persist (1.38x and 0.71x at the end). On seed 13 the starved daughter first absorbs a neighbour and then falls below 10% at t=691, 256 t after the fork. After the first dip, the following disk hops onto other bodies, as c18 reports.

observations.I: rerun/seed11/tracks.png: bodies keep a compact orange/cyan core inside their own ring for 100-280 t (#14, #87)
observations.M: rerun/seed11 and seed12 FACTS: 48/56 tracks move >= 1 body length, max 9.9/13.0 body lengths; forks/f11.png fed row: the daughter glides across the domain
observations.E: forks/summary.txt: starved daughter below 20% at fork+138 (s11), 0 at fork+134 (s12), below 10% at fork+256 after a merge (s13); the fed twins' same daughters persist; ledger drift < 1e-11
observations.D: rerun/seed11/lineage.png: 12 persistent splits to generation 5 from one planted patch; seed 12: 8 splits, generation 4

seeds_run.result: pass: gen 5, merge/split 0.76; fork: starved daughter to 19% at fork+138, fed twin persists
pass: gen 4, merge/split 0.86; fork: starved daughter to 0 at fork+134, fed twin persists
fork only: pass but confounded, the starved daughter merges with a neighbour and dies at fork+256

controls_run.E: forks/f11-f13: fed twin from the identical fork state vs a 9 px food-free disk that follows one daughter (c18's dfork.py, unchanged)

verdicts.limitation: S is grown where a ring convolution of the body density hits a set point, a band-pass readout of the body (RUBRIC L3), so B is by construction. Its only work is c18's speed effect, which I did not re-run. Neighbouring shells fuse into networks, and the genealogy is reticulate (merge/split 0.76-0.86), so D is capped at medium. Building matter from food is by construction; the fork is what makes E count, and the 9 px food-free disk would starve any blob of this matter. The planted patch means no S.
